- DEPTH 2, AND THE MESSAGE IS THE GAME'S OWN: 'You enter a maze of down staircases.' The character went down with 33 of 33 hit points, 7 of 7 spell points, 19 flasks of oil, 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, armour class 12 and no escape at all. What depth 2 is worth to a druid at character level 4 is the experience: the award is monster experience times the monster's level times nothing, divided by my level, so on depth 2 a kill is worth twice what it is worth on depth 1 - a small kobold is 2.5 units instead of 1.25, a giant black ant 4 instead of 2 - and character level 5 needs 36 more units for this High-Elf. So about ten ordinary kills on depth 2 is a level, and that is the first time in four lives this character has been anywhere near being able to level. (ask 843)
- THE SWEEP WALKED THE CHARACTER INTO A SOLDIER AND IT COST TWENTY-SIX HIT POINTS. A soldier at depth 2 is 23 hit points and two blows of 1d7 - up to fourteen damage a round against armour class 12, which is almost nothing - and my chain planner treats a letter as a monster only where it can SEE the letter, so a monster that came round a corner was walked into. The character is now at 7 of 33 with a soldier one tile south, and the two things that save a druid in this position are the potion and the staircase: QUAFFING applies its effect before the monsters take their turn, so the twenty points arrive before the fourteen land, while ASCENDING is also safe but throws the level away. Quaff first, and note for the next life: on depth 2 the planner must treat the neighbourhood of a letter as dangerous, not just the letter itself. (ask 846)
- THE SOLDIER'S NUMBERS, FROM THE GAME'S OWN DATA, AND WHY THE WHIP IS HOPELESS: depth 2 has four 'p' monsters - soldier (23 hp, armour class 24, two blows of 1d7), cutpurse (20 hp, AC 18, 1d6 and steals gold), acolyte (18 hp, AC 15, 1d5) and apprentice (15 hp, AC 9, 1d4) - all worth 6 experience, so three experience units a kill at character level four. A whip at to-hit 19 needs to-hit 16 to touch an armour class of 24 at all, so the best it can do against a soldier is 25 per cent, and eight or nine hits of 1d3 is eight or nine rounds of fourteen damage: the character would die before the soldier did. THE ONE WEAPON A DRUID HAS THAT IGNORES ARMOUR IS STINKING CLOUD - twelve damage at character level four, radius two, PROJECT_PLAY not set so it cannot hit the caster, and it costs two spell points out of seven. The soldier is at half health, so one cloud should finish it and the character should not lose a single hit point. (ask 848)
- THE CAST PROMPT IS WORTH A NOTE: 'm' then the book's pack letter opens 'Cast which verse?', and the list is the book's whole contents with level, mana cost, failure chance and effect - Detect Life (1 sp, 9 per cent), Fox Form (1 sp, 6 per cent), Remove Hunger (2 sp, 14 per cent), Stinking Cloud (2 sp, 19 per cent, damage 12, radius 2), Confuse Monster (3 sp, 28 per cent), Slow Monster (4 sp, 31 per cent). So the four spells this druid can cast now are known, their mana costs are known, and the failure chances are 6 to 31 per cent, which is the number no manual gives: a druid's best weapon fails a fifth of the time. Aiming at the acolyte's own square rather than at myself puts the ball exactly on it, and the caster is inside the radius but PROJECT_PLAY is not set on a player-cast BALL, so the druid is safe at point-blank range. (ask 850)
- STINKING CLOUD IS WORTH EVERY SPELL POINT A DRUID HAS: two spell points, twelve damage that ignores armour class, radius two, and it never touches the caster. It hit the acolyte and the cutpurse at once, because both were inside the radius, and the message is the death message - 'cries out feebly' - so a level-2 'p' dies to one cloud where the whip would have needed eight hits and taken twenty damage doing it. TWO SPELL POINTS AND NO HIT POINTS IS THE WHOLE FIGHT. The measure that matters is damage per hit point spent, and for this class the spell is roughly five times better than the weapon. (ask 851)
- POISON RESISTANCE IS A NUMBER, AND IT MATTERS: the acolyte went from half health to a tenth on a cloud that does twelve damage, so it took about seven - it resists a good deal of poison but not all of it, and the game says so in the message. THE CAST PROMPT IS A CHAIN: 'm' the book's pack letter, the verse letter, then the direction - 'mad2' is the whole spell in one ask, and the mana went from seven to five with two points spent. So a druid's best weapon is two spell points and one key, and it does not depend on armour class at all: a cloud that halves against a resistant monster still does more than the whip's best hit, and it costs no hit points and no time. (ask 852)
- THE ACOLYTE DIED AND NXT WENT FROM 25 TO 22 - three experience units, which is the first experience this character has earned on a dungeon level in four lives. The cloud cost two spell points and no hit points at all, and the character is still at 24 of 33 after two of them: the weapon that decided the fight was worth nothing in hit points, and the whip would have cost thirty. The acolyte dropped something - there is a '!' on the floor two tiles south of me, and a '!' is either a flask of oil or a potion and the text screen cannot tell them apart, so it has to be looked at before it is picked up. (ask 853)
- THE POLICY FOR AN UNKNOWN SCROLL, AND WHY I AM NOT READING IT YET: the manual says try one at full hit points, with nothing in view, standing on a staircase you could take, and the character is at twenty of thirty-three with a 'p' one tile away and one spell point out of seven. The pool on depth 2 is the same eight kinds: five fifty-weight ones, Deep Descent at twenty, Summon Monster and Darkness at ten each - so seven per cent of the pool drops the character five levels below its deepest onto no staircase at all, which from depth two is depth seven, with no Phase Door and no Recall. The rest comes first. THE PACK LETTERS ARE NOW KNOWN: the quaff prompt and the oil message together give them - a is the Lesser Charms book, b the rations, c the twenty flasks of oil, d the four Potions of Cure Light Wounds - so the next life of this character can use a scroll without spending an ask to find out which letter it is. (ask 855)
- RESTING NEXT TO A MONSTER IS NOT RESTING: the acolyte is one tile away and the rest ended on the first turn with a hit for four, so the character is at sixteen of thirty-three and the lesson is the one in the manual - rest only when no awake monster can reach you in about five turns - and the price of learning it was four hit points. THE QUAFF PROMPT IS TWO KEYS AND THE LETTER IS KNOWN: 'q' then 'd', because the prompt reads 'Quaff which potion? (Inven: d-d, ESC)' and the potions are at d. The same trick works for every menu in this game once the letter is known, and a family that has spent five lives writing down that the letters have to be read off the screen has never noticed that after the first reading they can be written down. (ask 856)
- A -more- SWALLOWED THE FIRST KEY OF THE LAST ASK, so the character did not move and did not pick up the scroll: the quaff message ended in -more- and my '4' went into it. My own rule says to end a key string with a space for exactly this reason and I did not do it. The rule is in the manual and it has cost this family five asks across three lives, so it is written here again where the next session will see it: A -more- SWALLOWS THE NEXT KEY, so any ask that follows a screen ending in -more- must begin with a space. (ask 858)
- A SCROLL OF PHASE DOOR, FOUND ON THE FLOOR OF DEPTH 2 AND IDENTIFIED THE MOMENT IT WAS PICKED UP - and this is the item the druid class has been missing for four lives, because the class has no teleport spell at any level and the manual says so outright: a Phase Door scroll is not a luxury for a druid, it is the weapon. It is fifteen gold in the alchemist's shop, it moves the caster about ten squares with no delay and no hit points, and a character that carries one can fight a soldier it cannot otherwise hurt. The fourth life of this character entered the dungeon with no Phase Door and no Recall because the second life spent two of them escaping Grip, and this life has spent its budget with two scrolls' worth of spells and one of them turned out to be the escape. THE ACOLYTE IS STILL ALIVE ONE TILE SOUTH AND THE WHIP STILL CANNOT KILL IT: 18 hit points at armour class 15, a whip at to-hit 19 hits it half the time, so it is six hits and twelve rounds of 1d5 - thirty hit points of damage for three experience units, which is a bad trade for a druid with two potions left. The cloud would do it for two spell points, and the character has one. (ask 859)
- THE THROW LIST HAS ITS OWN LETTERS, AND NOW THE PAIR IS SETTLED FOR THE FAMILY: the oil is c in the pack and a in the throw prompt, and the throw prompt's target is the closest monster with an apostrophe. A druid's whole fight is this one line of keys, and the reason the class needs it is the armour-class formula: hit_chance is 12 per cent plus 83 per cent of (to-hit minus two thirds of the target's armour class), so a thrown flask at to-hit 11 against the acolyte's armour class 15 is a 19 per cent shot at best, while the whip at to-hit 19 is 51 per cent - and the whip only does two to four damage a blow against eighteen hit points. Neither is good; the cloud is good, and the cloud costs two spell points the druid does not have. (ask 863)
- A WHITE HARPY IS BLOCKING THE ONLY WAY OUT, and the harpy is worth more than anything else on this level: ten experience, so five units at character level four, where a soldier is three. Its armour class is 24, so a whip at to-hit 19 reaches it at twenty-five per cent and a flask of oil at to-hit 11 reaches it at the twelve per cent floor, which is eight flasks for one harpy - the cheapest fight in the game is not a fight at all, it is two spell points of Stinking Cloud, and the character has one. The harpy bites for 1d3 and screams, and a screaming harpy is a bad thing to stand next to with no escape. So: the whip, twelve swings in one ask, and if the harpy is still alive at the end of it the Scroll of Phase Door is read off the floor and the character leaves the level by ten squares and loses the scroll that was two tiles away. (ask 865)
- THE PICK-UP KEY IS g AND ',' IS NOT: the manual lists ',' as 'stay a turn' and g as 'pick up', and I spent three decisions assuming otherwise, because an earlier life found that ',' picked a torch up IN LOOK MODE. So the two keys are different in different modes, which is the same trap as the throw prompt and the pack prompt having their own letters. The inventory screen afterwards showed no scroll, which is what proved the pick-up had failed rather than the scroll having been consumed. THE WHITE HARPY DIED IN TWELVE WHIP SWINGS for two experience units and two hit points of damage - the whip's twenty-five per cent against armour class 24 is a bad rate but a seven hit point target makes it cheap, and this is the second time in this life that a fight that looked hopeless in the manual turned out to be a fight the whip could win. The character now stands on the scroll's own square with the only exit open behind it. (ask 866)
- CHARACTER LEVEL 5 IS EIGHTEEN UNITS AWAY: the sheet says Cur Exp 84 and the level 5 threshold for a High-Elf is 101, and the fourth life of this character never got within thirty units of it because every one of its kills was on depth 1, where a kill is worth a quarter of an experience unit. On depth 2 the same kill is worth twice as much, so seven ordinary kills is a level, and that is the first time in four lives that this character has been able to see level 5 from where it stands. THE FULL REST IS FOUR KEYS: R, BACKSPACE, asterisk, ENTER. The rest prompt opens with '& ' already in the field, one backspace deletes the whole field, and the asterisk then means 'until hit points and spell points are full' - and the spell points are the point, because a druid's cloud costs two and the character has one, and a full rest is forty turns for two spell points. (ask 867)
- THE SPELL FAILED - 'You failed to concentrate hard enough!' - which is the nineteen per cent in the verse list being paid in one cast, and the cost of a failed cast is two spell points and no damage and nothing else. But THE ARMOUR CLASS WENT FROM 12 TO 20 IN THE SAME ASK, and nothing in this life explains it: the character was wearing Soft Leather Armour, a Metal Cap and a Cloak for 12, and the pack held no armour when I looked at it. A crow bit the character and there is a 'B' on the floor next to it, so something was picked up or put on that I did not do, and the only way to find out is to look at the equipment screen. Whichever it is, eight points of armour class is worth far more than the scroll that caused it, and this is a reminder that the screen's left panel is a report of the character and not of the player's intentions. (ask 869)
- THE EQUIPMENT SCREEN EXPLAINS NONE OF IT, and that is the finding: the character is wielding the whip, wearing Soft Leather Armour [8,+0], a Cloak [1,+0] and a Metal Cap [3,+0] - twelve points of armour class, exactly what it has worn all life - and the sidebar says Cur AC 20. Nothing is on the hands, the feet, the arms or the head but the metal cap, and the pack at the last look held a book, rations, oil, potions, a cloak and the Phase Door and no armour. So eight points of armour class arrived between two asks with no visible cause, and the only thing that happened in those two asks was a failed Stinking Cloud and a crow biting the character. The crows are 'B' and they are on the map beside the character and they are biting. A question worth asking of the source and not worth the rest of this life: does the crow - a 'B' - do something to the character's armour class when it bites, or did the character pick up something and put it on without the equipment screen being asked about it? Either way the character is better off than it was, and eight points of armour class is worth a great deal more than the scroll that may have caused it. (ask 871)
- FEAR IS A CONDITION THAT TAKES THE WEAPON AWAY, and no manual in this repository mentions it: 'You are too afraid to attack the crow!' means the character's attacks do not happen at all while the fear timer runs, so a character that is afraid and surrounded is a character that is being eaten and cannot fight back. The crow's scare blow put it there, and the two crows were biting it down from twenty-five to twenty-two hit points while it could do nothing. So the last potion goes first - a Cure Light Wounds is twenty points and the character is at twenty-two, which is a full character - and then the fear has had a turn to wear off. AND THE ARMOUR CLASS IS STILL 20 WITH NOTHING NEW ON, so it is not the fear and not the crows and not anything in the equipment list, which leaves the game doing something this family has not found before. (ask 874)
- THE FEAR WAS THE ARMOUR CLASS: while the character was afraid the sidebar said Cur AC 20, and the moment the fear ended - 'You feel bolder now.' - it went back to 12, with the equipment list unchanged the whole time. So being afraid gives a druid eight points of armour class, which is what makes a frightened character so hard to hit, and it is a bargain that looks like a gift and is not: fear blocks the character's attacks entirely ('You are too afraid to attack the crow!') and it cost this life twenty hit points and about eight decisions while two crows ate a character that could not hit back. A SCROLL OF REMOVE FEAR would be worth more to this class than a scroll of Phase Door, and the alchemist does not stock it. THE REST WORKED AS A CURE FOR NOTHING except that it let the timer run: ten turns of rest, two bites, and the fear ended on its own, so the fear in this game is a timer and the only thing that cures it is time. (ask 879)
- A HUNDRED AND FIFTEEN GOLD PIECES ON THE FLOOR OF DEPTH 2, and it is the single most valuable thing this character has ever held: the alchemist's Phase Door is fifteen, twenty flasks of oil are sixty, two Potions of Cure Light Wounds are forty, and a Scroll of Magic Mapping is sixty-five - so the pile is a whole escape ladder, a full oil supply, the healing this class needs and the scroll that four lives of this family have wanted to buy and could not. THE GOLD PILES ON DEPTH 2 ARE NOT WHAT THE AVERAGE SAYS: the average is nineteen and this one was a hundred and fifteen, so the wealth of a depth is as lumpy as its monsters are. And the character reached it with eight hit points, one spell point and no escape, which is the whole shape of this life: the interesting finds come on the far side of a fight that should not have been survived. (ask 890)

note: Depth 2 room decoded from the game data (vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/monster.txt): yellow mushroom patch = 1 hp, NEVER_MOVE, SPORE:TERRIFY:1d4 (the dice is the FEAR DURATION not damage), exp 2; grey MOLD (different from the grey mushroom patch!) = 2 hp, 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, exp 3, and it is MOBILE (speed 110, no NEVER_MOVE) so it can come to me; apprentice = 15 hp, AC 9, 1d4 melee, exp 6, spells BLIND|BLINK|CONF|MISSILE at spell-freq 12, and friends-base 20/40/80% summons 1d3 person companions when it dies. So an apprentice is a bad fight for a 13 HP CL1 druid: blink + blind + confuse is exactly what killed the Mage in NOTES.md, and killing it may spawn 1-3 more mages. DECISION: do not fight the apprentice or the grey mould; take the clear south door. Both hazardous monsters are in the far corners of the room, the south door is clear, and I need experience from something safer than this. (ask 174)

note: LOOK-MODE TRICK worth keeping: in look mode the cursor SNAPS to the next 'interesting' square (monster, item, door, staircase) in the direction pressed, skipping plain floor - one press of a direction enumerates the next thing along that line. Pressing the same direction again walks the cursor further along the same line (it does not restart from me), so 'l' then a direction repeated walks the whole line. That gives exact positions without any pixel-map reading, and it costs no turns: the room west of me enumerated as ant 5W, yellow patch 6W+1S, First Spells book 9W+1N, closed door 10W; east: grey mould 4E. (ask 197)

note: THROW MISSED the sleeping ant at distance 2 (ask 201: 'The giant black ant is targeted... The Flask of oil breaks' with NO damage line, and ask 205 confirms the ant is still 'unhurt, asleep'). Source reading (vendor/angband/src/player-attack.c): make_ranged_throw() applies the OF_EXPLODE x3 damage ONLY if test_hit() passed - a miss breaks the flask on the floor and does nothing. The hit chance is chance_of_missile_hit_base() minus distance, against the monster's AC. The ant's AC 24 (monster.txt) is brutal: hit_chance() needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have any chance above the flat 12% always-hit, so at range you are mostly rolling the 12%. (ask 205)

note: Studied Remove Hunger at ask 217: 'You have learned the verse of Remove Hunger.' and NXT stayed at 7 - so STUDYING a spell costs no experience; the exp field in class.txt (Detect Life 2, Fox Form 10, Remove Hunger 2) is the FIRST CAST cost, not the learning cost. So a druid must reach CL3 before Stinking Cloud can be learned, and 'Study (1)' means one verse per character level. (ask 217)

note: KEY ERROR OF MINE, worth recording so no next run repeats it: after pressing 'l' (look) the look mode STAYS ACTIVE and swallows the next command's first key. At asks 221-225 I sent 'l', then 'va\'', then 'va1' and nothing happened - the look descriptions ('You are on an open floor', 'You see a yellow mushroom patch') kept printing and no turn passed, because the keys were being read as look-mode cursor moves, not as 'throw'. The tell is that the turn counter did not move and the message line showed a LOOK description. Press '\e' to leave look mode before any other command. With look mode properly closed, 'va\'' works exactly as advertised: 'The yellow mushroom patch is targeted' / 'Your Flask of oil hits the yellow mushroom patch' / 'The yellow mushroom patch is destroyed' (2 exp, NXT 7 -> 5). The yellow patch was the reason the west corridor was lethal - adjacent to it you get TERRIFIED. (ask 229)

note: TWO OIL THROWS AT THE SMALL KOBOLD BOTH MISSED (asks 235, 236) and it hit me for 2 (HP 20/22). Its AC 24 against my throwing skill is the problem, not the damage: hit_chance() in player-attack.c needs to_hit >= ac*2/3 = 16 to have more than the flat 12% always-hit, and a throwing flask at range 1-2 lands around 30-60. LESSON: the depth-1 monsters that are worth killing with oil are the LOW-AC ones (white worm mass AC 1, grey mould AC 1, yellow patch AC 1, mouse AC 4, centipede AC 12-14). A small kobold (AC 24) and a giant black ant (AC 24) are oil targets only from 1 tile away. The giant black ant died from range 1 with one flask; the same flask at range 2 missed. (ask 237)

note: GLYPH TABLE now decoded from vendor/angband/lib/gamedata/terrain.txt (each 'graphics:<char>:<colour>' line): space=unknown grid, .=open floor, +=closed door, '=open door (u=broken), <=UP staircase, >=DOWN staircase, 1-8=stores, #=secret door or granite/permanent wall or lava, :=pile of rubble, %=MAGMA VEIN or QUARTZ VEIN (a solid wall - the colour tells them apart, a text dump cannot), *=vein with treasure. So the corridor I am in is a vein-walled passage: the '%' above and below me are walls, not floor, and the fact that they are drawn '%' and not '#' only tells me they are rock veins. note: THE '[' COMMAND IS THE BEST ONE-ASK SCAN IN THE GAME: it prints 'You can see N monsters:' with the glyph, the COUNT, the name and the exact relative position of each - e.g. 'c 1 giant yellow centipede 2 S 0 W' (ask 245). That is a monster-list panel with the relative offset, so a player who cannot use the map can still know exactly what is around and how far. It even offers 'Press x to turn ON sort by exp'. Combined with 'l' (look) in a direction, which snaps the cursor to the next interesting square and reports 'N N, E W', I can reconstruct the local geometry without ever reading a pixel of the map. (ask 245)

note: Found and picked up an UNIDENTIFIED scroll on depth 2 (ask 273), title 'imusto que', dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet. Deep Descent has level:10 and alloc:20:1 to 100 in object.txt, so at CL2 it is exactly this: a scroll with a random title that only identifies at level 10. Reading it at CL2 is what the knowledge in NOTES.md says to do (unknown consumables at CL1-3 are worth trying; the first use pays a little experience). If it is Deep Descent it drops me 5 levels below my deepest level reached - depth 2 + 5 = depth 7. Worst plausible case is Summon Monster (cost:0, alloc:10) or Darkness or Blessing. Word of Recall is the way home if depth 7 goes badly (read in the dungeon = town, 15-34 turns). (ask 274)

note: The unidentified scroll on depth 2 turned out to be a Scroll of LIGHT, not Deep Descent: 'You are surrounded by a white light' then 'You have no more Scrolls of Light (g)'. So it identified at first use and cost no experience (NXT stayed at 2) - Light's exp field in class.txt/object.txt is small. Harmless, and now known. What I can say about the DROP: it was dropped by a small kobold at 100 feet (level 2), so a depth-2 kobold carried a Scroll of Light - the monster drop table is a real source of consumables, and killing a monster is a way to GET a scroll rather than hoping to find one on the floor. (ask 277)

note: DECISIVE TEST of the manual's 'l>g' recipe: in look mode press '>' and the cursor jumps to the nearest KNOWN down staircase (vendor/angband/src/ui-target.c, path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs). On depth 2 at ask 284 I tried it and there is NO known down staircase anywhere in the level I have explored - so the recipe cannot help until a '>' glyph has actually been seen. That is the real reason 'no run has ever found a down staircase': not that the staircases are rare, but that the game's own jump only works on a staircase you already know about. The way to know about one is to LOOK at the glyph (the 'l' command named it for me on depth 1: 'You see a down staircase, 1 S, 1 W'), so a player who reads every glyph on every map has a chance and a player who trusts the frontier logic does not. (ask 284)

note: SOURCE ANSWER to the repo's standing question 'is the down staircase findable at all': NO SPATIAL RULE EXISTS. gen-cave.c:1583 allocates exactly ONE down staircase per level (alloc_stairs(c, FEAT_MORE, 1, 0, ...)), gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with exactly 3 adjacent walls, and cave_find_get_grid() (gen-util.c:202) picks that square by random choice over the WHOLE level (state[] holds every square in the level and the next one is drawn with randint0). So the down staircase is uniform over the level's floor squares - there is no 'it is near the up staircase' or 'it is in the biggest room' heuristic to exploit. The level is 198x66 with up to 50 rooms (dungeon_profile.txt 'classic' params:11:50:200:2), and the map window is 36x22, so a level is about five screens wide and three tall. Finding one by walking is a matter of covering thousands of squares; the previous run's 148 asks and my 140 have not come close. The reliable routes are a Deep Descent scroll or a Magic Mapping scroll, and neither was available to me. (ask 289)

note: STINKING CLOUD SOURCE READING (effect-handler-attack.c:594, effect_handler_BALL): the flags are PROJECT_THRU|PROJECT_STOP|PROJECT_GRID|PROJECT_ITEM|PROJECT_KILL and PROJECT_PLAY is NOT among them, and project() only affects the player when PROJECT_PLAY is set (project.c:519 and :996). So a druid's Stinking Cloud CANNOT hit the caster, even when the ball is centred on a monster 2 tiles away. That is a big deal for a 26 HP druid: the radius-2 poison ball is a safe weapon at point blank range. Damage = PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10 = 11 poison at CL3, halved with distance from the centre. (ask 310)

note: THE FIGHT WITH GRIP, measured: it bites for 2-4 a turn against my AC 12 (much less than its 1d4 suggests, because AC 12 cuts most of the small dice), and it WAKES me if I try to rest - but a counted rest ('R' then a number) runs the full count anyway, taking the hits as they come. Spell points are the bottleneck, not hit points: 4 turns of rest bought no SP at all, so ~10+ turns of rest are needed for 1 SP. Stinking Cloud is the only weapon that can hurt it (AC 36 - a flask of oil at point blank MISSED, and so did one against the kobold at AC 24). Two casts of 11 poison would finish its remaining ~17 hp. (ask 323)

note: ESCAPE LADDER in practice, measured: against Grip (AC 36, 25 hp, +10 speed, biting me for 2-4 a turn in a one-wide corridor) I could not fight it - a flask of oil at point blank missed, my whip has a 12 percent chance against AC 36, and the spell that CAN hurt it costs 2 SP while I had 1. THE SPELL POINT ECONOMY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, and the source explains it: player-util.c:487 player_regen_mana() computes sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE, with PY_REGEN_NORMAL = 197 and PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 524, both in 65536ths (player-util.h:27,31), and doubled while resting. For msp = 5 that is about 0.023 SP per turn, so ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of rest, and a Stinking Cloud needs two. Resting beside Grip for 90 turns is not a plan. So the Phase Door scroll is not a luxury - with a 2 SP weapon and no melee that reaches, the scroll IS the weapon. (ask 327)

note: GREY MOULD KILLED at range 1 with one flask (2 hp, AC 1 - a certain hit at that range, 3 experience). The mould was the one monster on this level that could actually reach and hurt me: it is MOBILE (no NEVER_MOVE flag, unlike the mushroom patches) and it does 2 x SPORE:HURT:1d4, so up to 8 damage a turn against my AC 12. It bit me while I was trying to read a scroll, which is worth knowing: a spell or scroll takes a turn, and the turn the spell resolves on is a turn the monster also acts. (ask 348)

note: THE BEST SCANNING TOOL IN THE GAME, found by accident: cast Detect Life and then press '['. The detection sets MFLAG_SHOW on every living monster within 22 rows x 40 columns (effect-handler-general.c detect_monsters), and the '[' list then shows a SECOND section headed 'You are aware of N monsters:' with the glyph, count, name, sleep state and the exact relative position of each - including monsters that are out of sight and were not in the 'You can see' list. At ask 361 that gave me: Grip 5 S 3 W, a green worm mass (asleep) 17 S 3 W, and TWO giant yellow centipedes (2 asleep) - all invisible to the eye and all on the map. This is worth more than the spell's own effect: the spell is the only thing in the game that gives a player a monster list over a 22x40 area, and the manual never says so. (ask 361)

note: SPELL POINT ECONOMY MEASURED, and it is the single most important number for a druid: with msp = 5 at CL3, player_regen_mana() gives sp_gain = msp * PY_REGEN_NORMAL + PY_REGEN_MNBASE = 5*197 + 524 = 1509 in 65536ths = 0.023 spell points per turn, doubled to about 0.046 while resting. So ONE spell point costs roughly 22 turns of RESTING and 43 turns of not resting, and a Stinking Cloud needs two of them. I rested 20 turns and gained nothing at all (SP stayed 1/5, HP went to 26/26). For a class whose only good spell costs 2 SP, the spell book is nearly decorative until the character can afford to sit still for a minute of game time. (ask 363)

note: GRIP KILLED at ask 367: 'Grip, Farmer Maggot's Dog, dies. Welcome to level 4.' Three flasks of oil in total against it, two of them hitting, at ranges 1 and 2. That is the whole recipe for a DL2 unique as a CL3 druid: never melee it (my whip is 1d3+1 at to-hit 19 against its AC 36 - a 12 percent chance), never rely on the spell (2 spell points that take 43 turns of rest to earn), and just throw oil from range until one lands. It gave 30 experience and took me from NXT 12 to level 4. Final state: depth 2, CL4, 26/26 HP, 1/5 SP, 24 flasks of oil, 3 Cure Light Wounds, 1 Scroll of Word of Recall, AC 12, and no down staircase found on depth 2. (ask 367)

note: CL4, HP 26/33, SP 1/7, NXT 28 (so CL5 needs 28 more). Studied Fox Form at CL4: the spell list at CL4 is Detect Life (1 sp), Fox Form (2 sp), Remove Hunger (2 sp), Stinking Cloud (2 sp, 'dam 12, rad 2' now that I know it - it was 11 at CL3, so the poison scales with level as class.txt says: PLAYER_LEVEL/2 + 10). Confuse Monster is CL5 and Slow Monster CL6, so neither is available yet. Fox Form (shape.txt: combat:-3:-3:3 = -3 to-hit, -3 to-dam, +3 AC; STR[-3], BLOWS[1], MOVES[1], FREE_ACT, FEATHER) is the druid's only intrinsic escape, and I had just been chased by a +10 speed dog that I could only fight with oil. Its costs are real: -3 to my already weak whip, -3 STR, 10 experience on the first cast, and no items while shaped (no quaffing a Cure Light Wounds while a fox). (ask 370)

note: Testing the Word of Recall, which no run in this repo has ever used: read in the dungeon it sets a timer (player->word_recall = randint0(20) + 15 turns, effect-handler-general.c:1141) and when it expires it takes you to town ('You feel yourself yanked upwards!', game-world.c:709-727). The timer is NOT interrupted by damage - it is a plain countdown - so it is only a safe way home when nothing is chasing you, which is exactly why c15 ESC-04 does not count it as an escape. (ask 374)

note: WORD OF RECALL VERIFIED, and it is better than the manual says. Read in the dungeon: 'The air about you becomes charged...', the status line then shows 'Recall' between Light and Fed, and after the timer expires 'You feel yourself yanked upwards!' and the depth becomes 0 (town). The timer ran about 26 turns (turn 10252 to 10501) and was NOT interrupted by anything - I simply rested through it. Crucially, arriving in town HEALED ME TO FULL (28/33 -> 33/33) and gave back 2 spell points, because town has no monsters and the character regenerates there. So the scroll is not an escape (c15 ESC-04 is right - the delay is too long to survive a chase) but it IS a free full heal and a free trip to the shops when nothing is chasing you. (ask 381)

note: BLACK MARKET (store 7) STOCK ON SEED 23, the shop the previous run never visited: Lo-Hak the Awful (Half-Troll). Wand of Stun Monster (5 charges) 1875, Staff of Curing (7 charges) 2025, Lantern of Brightness (7500 turns) 3150, 11 Robes [2,+0] 42, 3 Sets of Gauntlets [3,+0] 72, Trident of Slay Animal (1d10) (+5,+7) 4902, 10 Arrows of Wounding (1d4) (+9,+13) 309. NO Deep Descent and NO Magic Mapping. The reason is in the source: store_create_random() in store.c picks the Black Market's stock as a random object of level player->max_depth + 5 to + 20 (so level 7 to 22 for me at depth 2), and the price is 150 percent of the true value (store.c:617) - the Deep Descent's base cost is 250, so it would have been about 375 and hopeless on 26 gold anyway. The cheapest useful thing there is a robe of +2 AC for 42 gold. (ask 384)

note: ALCHEMIST STOCK ON SEED 23, LATER IN THE DAY - and it answers the previous run's open question: 'Magic Mapping 65 g did not help' and 'the Alchemist did not stock one this seed'. The Alchemist RESTOCKS EVERY DAY and rolls a fresh stock from its normal list, and the shopkeeper itself changes (Mauser the Chemist / Wizzle the Chaotic / Ga-nat the Greedy / Vella the Slender). At ask 399, under Vella the Slender, the stock was: 40 Potions of Cure Light Wounds 20, Potion of Cure Serious Wounds 70, 5 Potions of Cure Critical Wounds 200, Potion of Restore Life Levels 400, 2 Potions of Berserk Strength 80, 40 Scrolls of Phase Door 15, 3 Scrolls of Magic Mapping 65, 40 Scrolls of Remove Curse 100, 40 Scrolls of Word of Recall 125, 3 Scrolls of Recharging 200, 9 Scrolls of Holy Chant 40. SO MAGIC MAPPING IS FOR SALE - three of them - for 65 gold. I could not buy it: a street urchin stole 8 of my 26 gold in town and I was down to 18. The lesson for the next run is sharp: BUY THE MAGIC MAPPING SCROLL FIRST, in the Alchemist, on whichever day it is in stock, and go back to town for it - a level of gold spent here saves 200 asks of blind exploration. The stock rolls when the game day changes (store.c store_maint is called once per daycount, and the shopkeeper shuffles on a 1-in-z_info->store_shuffle chance per day). (ask 399)

note: At ask 412 the same street urchin stole 15 more gold while walking west: AU 18 to 3, while the run went from town (70,15) to (60,15). This repeats ask 394's 8-gold theft and confirms town thieves can strip nearly all carried gold during a long movement. The countermeasure is not available because selling pays zero, so the practical rule is: do not carry gold while roaming; spend it before walking far, and return to a shop tile when a thief is nearby. (ask 412)

note: At ask 427 the game's look-mode jump worked in TOWN: 'l>' said 'You recall a down staircase, 5 N, 9 E.' and the next 'g' began walking toward it. After manual navigation I reached the town down staircase at ask 436 (cursor 40,4, status 'Down staircase'). This confirms the inherited note's l>g recipe is useful even in town, where the staircase is already known; the earlier inherited report had focused on dungeon stairs. Town thieves also cost 15 gold during this walk (18 to 3 at ask 412), and repeated dog/rogue attacks took HP from 32 to 16 by ask 435. (ask 436)

note: THREE NEW MECHANICS, all measured this life: (1) The '>' jump to a KNOWN down staircase works in LOOK mode ('l>') as well as in targeting mode ('*>'): do_cmd_look (ui-knowledge.c:4169) calls target_set_interactive(TARGET_LOOK, -1, -1, true), and that last true is allow_pathfinding, so look mode is a targeting mode and handles '>', '<' and 'g' exactly as the manual says. I first wrote the opposite because 'l>' produced NO MESSAGE on a level with no known staircase - the failure path is bell() (ui-target.c:1506), and a bell draws no text in a text dump. The manual was right and this note was wrong: a silent screen is what a failed jump looks like, not a missing key. (2) Pressing '>' when NOT standing on a staircase prints 'I see no down staircase here.' and does NOT auto-navigate: do_cmd_go_down (cmd-cave.c:106) only falls through to do_cmd_navigate_down if the option autoexplore_commands is set, and it is OFF by default. (3) The targeting cursor IS drawn as a literal '*' in the map, so a plain-text player can SEE the cursor move - at ask 480 '*x' put the cursor on the tile 1 N of me. The 'x' key is path_nearest_unknown (nearest unexplored square); '>' is path_nearest_known(square_isdownstairs); both need the staircase to be KNOWN, so on a fresh level there is nothing for '>' to jump to. (ask 481)

note: THE ESCAPE LADDER IS GONE. The pack at ask 492 holds exactly six items: a) Book of Nature Magics [Lesser Charms], b) 2 Rations, c) 23 Flasks of oil, d) 1 Potion of Cure Light Wounds, e) a Wooden Torch (3920 turns), f) a Cloak [1,+0]. There is NO Phase Door scroll and NO Word of Recall left - not stolen, SPENT: the prior life burned its Phase Door scrolls to escape (notebook ask 333) and read the Word of Recall to come home (ask 381, which also healed to full). The prior life's own REPORT says it ended with '22 flasks of oil, 1 Cure Light Wounds, 18 gold'. So the druid now has oil and a whip and nothing else: no scroll escape, no recall, no healing beyond one potion. What remains is: oil (46 lb of a ~108 lb budget), one CLW, and 3 gold with the shops out of reach. This changes the plan for this life - the run cannot leave the dungeon except by dying or by reaching a down staircase and going DEEPER, and a bad fight on depth 2-3 with no Phase Door is likely fatal. (ask 492)

note: THE FASTEST EXPLORATION LOOP IN THE GAME, and it is in the manual only as a footnote: in TARGETING mode ('*') the digit keys move the CURSOR, not the player, and 'x' then 'g' will walk you to the nearest unexplored square to wherever the cursor is. Because the cursor is clamped to the level bounds (cave->width-2, cave->height-2) and 'x' is path_nearest_unknown(CURSOR), you can aim the cursor 40+ tiles into ground you have never seen and the pathfinder will then walk there THROUGH UNKNOWN TERRAIN, revealing it as it goes (find_path in player-path.c:1069 falls back from known-only to any-grid when the destination is unknown). Measured: '*~30 digits in one direction' + 'x' + 'g' walked 17 tiles and 170 turns on one ask (ask 520) and then 29 tiles and 290 turns on the next (ask 522). The digit keys move the cursor ONE tile per press, not the 10 that is_running_keymap() would give - the running-keymap test at ui-target.c:1617 did not fire for plain digits. So the recipe is: '*' then N repetitions of a digit direction, then 'x', then 'g'. The 'g' leaves targeting mode (ui-target.c:1488 sets done = true) so each ask is ONE walk. This is how a level of 198x66 can be covered at all: the plain '*xg' loop only advances the frontier by one tile per ask. (ask 522)

note: THREE MORE THINGS MEASURED, and the first is the most useful command in the game for a plain-text player. (1) THE CURSOR-MOVE EXPLORATION LOOP: in targeting mode ('*') the digit keys move the CURSOR one tile per press, and 'x' then 'g' walks you to the nearest UNEXPLORED square to wherever the cursor is. But the far better version DROPS the 'x': '*' plus N repetitions of a direction digit, then 'g' alone, asks the game to pathfind to that exact grid, and find_path() (player-path.c:1069) falls back from a known-only path to one through unknown grids when the destination is unknown - so the walk goes THROUGH unexplored ground and reveals it. Measured walks this life: 170 turns (17 tiles), 290 turns (29 tiles), 310, 320, 330, 390 and 440 turns (22 tiles) on single asks, and the aim has to be BIG (30-70 tiles) or the destination lands in a wall and nothing happens at all. Two consecutive 'x'+'g' legs in one answer cancel each other: 'g' sets done=true and leaves targeting mode (ui-target.c:1488), and the next key then cancels the run - so one walk per ask is the real limit. (2) THE GREY MUSHROOM PATCH IS THE WORST MONSTER ON DEPTH 1: monster.txt gives it 2 hp, AC 1, NEVER_MOVE, blow SPORE:CONFUSE:1d4 - the 1d4 is the CONFUSION DURATION and it deals 1 damage a turn as well. Confusion is the single most crippling condition in the game: it blocks CASTING (player-util.c:1103 'You are too confused!'), blocks running and exploring (cmd-cave.c:1503), and randomises every direction you give - movement, attack and throw - with 75 percent probability (player_confuse_dir, player-util.c:1353), so you attack walls and throw oil at nothing. A Cure Light Wounds cures it for 20 turns and is worth more than its 20 healing when one is carrying. A melee whip at AC 1 kills the patch in one blow, and the whip's direction is randomised too, so twelve 'whip hits' in one answer make a hit very likely. Stinking Cloud hits it but the patch 'resists a lot' - every monster has IM_POIS. (3) THE ENTER KEY IS CARRIAGE RETURN, not newline: 'R50' followed by \n leaves the rest prompt sitting there with '50' in it and no turn passes; the same command with \r rests 500 turns. That cost me three asks. (ask 606)

note: THE DEPTH 1 OF THIS SEED IS A DIFFERENT LEVEL FROM THE ONE THE PRIOR LIVES WALKED, and that is worth recording because it settles a question the notebook had left open. The prior life found a down staircase on depth 1 at ask 161 and descended; this life, after the Word of Recall sent it to town and back down at ask 437, found a DIFFERENT depth 1: the terrain is different (no '%' vein corridors at all, where the old level had them), the up staircase sits in a different place, and the game's own '>' jump to a KNOWN down staircase (path_nearest_known with square_isdownstairs, which requires square_isknown) finds nothing here - so the staircase the character descended is not merely unseen here, it is not remembered here either. The level was regenerated on the way back up. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANYBODY WHO CONTINUES THIS CHARACTER: the down staircase of depth 1 must be found again from scratch, and the only route that works is LOOKING at every glyph on every map, because the game's own tools ('>' for a known staircase, Magic Mapping, Detect Stairs) all require that the staircase already be known or the scroll be owned. OVER 174 SCREENS OF THIS LEVEL (the final count; the figure when the note was written was 171) I NEVER SAW A '>' GLYPH, and the level is 198x66 with exactly one down staircase placed uniformly at random over its floor (gen-cave.c:1583 allocates one; gen-util.c:620 places it on a square with three adjacent walls). THE SHAPE OF THE LEVEL I DID MAP, for whoever comes next: a long east-west corridor on one row running most of the width of the level, with the up staircase near its middle, rooms off it to the north and south, two LOCKED DOORS (one 1 north of the corridor near the up staircase, one 4 north and 4 east of it) whose rooms are entered only by picking the lock (Searching 26 percent, so expect three or four tries), several grey mushroom patches near the doors, and a large open chamber to the north-west reached by the corridor at its north end. The '>' is not in any of the rooms I entered. (ask 607)

note: THE AIMED WALK, first measured this life: '*' then 40 x '8' (north) then 'g', no 'x'. The cursor clamps to the level bounds, so a 40-tile aim lands at the top edge; the path itself is computed by find_path (player-path.c:1107) where only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest), so an UNKNOWN destination makes unknown grids passable and the path crosses unexplored terrain. Whether that walk is long or a bogus short one is the disagreement between my own lives 2 and 3 (minimaxflash-2 said unknown destinations give a short meaningless path; minimaxflash-1.3 measured 17-29 tile walks with exactly this recipe). The turn counter on the next screen settles it. (ask 611)

note: M SCALES THE WHOLE LEVEL, and this corrects three lives of my own notes. display_map (src/ui-map.c:761) computes row = (y * map_hgt) / cave->height and col = (x * map_wid) / cave->width for EVERY square of the level, so the M panel is a scaled picture of the entire 198x66 level, not a window into it. My notes said 'M is a window onto the level' and 'M shows only the remembered region'; the second half is right (map_info reads cave->memory, so unexplored squares are blank) but the first half is wrong - it is the whole level, scaled to 78x22. So M is the orientation tool I never had: it shows my absolute position on the level and the whole explored region at once. (ask 622)

note: A FAILED LOCK PICK CANCELS THE REST OF THE KEY STRING, and that is the rule I needed: the message is 'You failed to pick the lock. Cancelled.' - Cancelled is the game's run-cancel message, so the remaining presses are eaten. A locked door therefore gets ONE pick attempt per ask, not one per press, and a digit string of repeats is useless against a lock. THE CHANCE IS IN THE SOURCE: calc_unlocking_chance (player-calcs.c:1676) returns MAX(2, skill - 4 * lock_power), the door's lock level is randint1(7) (gen-util.c:581) and a CL4 High-Elf Druid has SKILL_DISARM_PHYS = 30 + 10*3 + 4 = 64, so the chance is 36 to 60 percent - one attempt in two on average, not the 26 percent my notebook claimed. The skill is divided by ten if no_light(player), i.e. if the player's own square is dark. (ask 624)

note: THE AIMED WALK IS SHORT WHEN THE DESTINATION IS UNKNOWN, and the reason is now clear from the source: find_path treats unknown grids as passable, so the path to a far unknown aim is a straight line through ground nobody has seen, and the walk stops at the first REAL wall. The walk I aimed 25 tiles north moved me two tiles and aborted. A digit string along KNOWN floor is the reliable way to cover distance, and 'lxg' (jump to the nearest unexplored square) is the reliable way to extend the frontier, because its destination is adjacent to ground already seen. So the sweep is a sequence of planned digit strings along known corridors, each ending by probing north into the dark. (ask 626)

note: CORRECTION TO MY OWN LAST NOTE, and a finding worth more than the correction: '!' IS AMBIGUOUS IN A TEXT DUMP. object.txt gives the oil kind graphics:!:y AND gives the potions graphics:!:d, and the only difference is the colour, which a plain-text player never sees. So a '!' on the floor may be a flask of oil or a potion, and the only way to tell is to look at it or to pick it up: what I picked up was 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, which is the potion the character has been without for two lives. The druid now has oil, four heals and two unidentified scrolls, and no longer has to fight anything it cannot walk away from. (ask 638)

note: WHETHER THE AIMED WALK FINDS NEW GROUND DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE DESTINATION IS KNOWN, and that resolves the disagreement between my own lives two and three. find_path sets only_known = square_isknown(start) && square_isknown(dest), so an aim that lands on a square I have already seen is pathed over remembered ground only and the walk is a stroll along corridors I have walked; an aim that lands on a square I have NOT seen is pathed through unknown ground, which the pathfinder treats as passable, and the walk crosses new territory as it goes. So the rule is: aim further than the edge of what you know. From level column 154 the known ground stops at 124, so a 45-tile aim lands 31 tiles into the dark. (ask 661)

note: THE KEYPAD IS CONFIRMED FROM THE SOURCE and my slip was mine alone: ddx and ddy are indexed by the digit itself (cave.c: ddx = 0,-1,0,1,-1,0,1,-1,0,1 and ddy = 0,1,1,1,0,0,0,-1,-1,-1), so 4 is left, 6 is right, 8 is up, 2 is down, and target_dir_allow turns a digit into that index with D2I. So the aimed walk's direction is exactly what I ask for; what I do not control is the route. Two measurements in a row of the same recipe gave 33 tiles and 3 tiles, and both times the pathfinder went somewhere I did not point, because with an unknown destination it treats every unseen square as passable and the cheapest route to a point in the dark is not the straight one. (ask 662)

note: THE PANEL'S COLUMN SHIFT IS A TRAP FOR A READER, and I fell into it twice: the map's left edge is drawn behind the sidebar, so on a row whose sidebar text is one character short every glyph on that row is one column out. Two of my own maps disagreed with each other about where I was standing, and the only reliable position is the one on the M map, which is drawn on its own grid and not over a sidebar. So: the M map for where I am, look.py for what is next to me, and never a column number off a raw screen row. (ask 667)

note: LOOK MODE IS THE NAVIGATOR I FORGOT I HAD: in look mode a direction key does not move the cursor one tile, it SNAPS it to the next interesting square in that direction - a door, a monster, an item, a staircase - and the message line then names it with its exact offset. So 'l' then a direction then 'g' is one ask to walk to the next door on the level, with the game doing the geometry and telling me what it found. That is worth more than the aimed walk, which spends an ask to go three tiles. (ask 672)

That is worth recording because the whole of this run's money problem was solved by three gold and a shop three hundred columns away - but it also says the way to buy a Magic Mapping scroll or a Phase Door is to kill things, and killing on depth 1 pays almost no experience at character level 4. note: FIVE DIRECTION AIMED WALKS FROM ONE SPOT, measured: north 1 tile, north-west 0, north 3, west 26 (the wrong way), south-west 1. The aimed walk is a slot machine - it asks the pathfinder for the level's edge and the pathfinder answers with whatever route it believes is cheapest, and an unknown destination makes unknown squares free, so the route tends to be a straight line that a real wall stops. The look-mode snap is the reliable one and the digit string is the cheap one; the aimed walk is for when I want to cross a lot of known ground in one ask. (ask 677)

note: A SCROLL OF LIGHT IS WORTH MORE ON A SWEEP THAN IT LOOKS: the character's torch shows two tiles, so every step memorises about four squares of the level, and a permanent light globe would memorise a whole room in one turn. The two scrolls on the floor had the same title and turned out to be different kinds - one Blessing, one Light - so an unidentified object's title is not its kind, and the only way to know is to read it. A Scroll of Light costs nothing but a turn, and it makes the last hundred asks of this sweep cover much more ground. (ask 688)

note: READ BEFORE PLAYING (ask 754): I opened CONTINUEGAME.txt (all), AGENTS.md, docs/BRIEF.md (all), manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md (all), manuals/INSTRUCTIONS_2.md (all), my own playbook agents/minimax/COMMON.md (all) and agents/minimax/DRUID.md (all), my own four write-ups runs/minimaxflash-1/REPORT.md, runs/minimaxflash-1-again/REPORT.md, runs/minimaxflash-1.3/REPORT.md and runs/minimaxflash-1.4/REPORT.md, my inherited notebook runs/minimaxflash-1.5/notebook.md, and in vendor/angband the source and data for the questions I had: src/gen-cave.c, src/gen-util.c, src/ui-map.c and lib/gamedata/{dungeon_profile,terrain}.txt. NOT read: any other run's decisions, report or notebook, PLAN.md, ACCUMULATED_KNOWLEDGE.md. || THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE PLAN. (1) THE GENERATOR PUTS THREE OR FOUR DOWN STAIRCASES ON A DEPTH-1 LEVEL, NOT ONE: gen-cave.c:1291 inside classic_gen (and modified_gen at :2939) calls handle_level_stairs(c, ..., rand_range(3, 4), rand_range(1, 2)) - the source comment itself says 'Place 3 or 4 down stairs and 1 or 2 up stairs near some walls'. The 'exactly one down staircase' claim in my own DRUID.md and in minimaxflash-1.4's report came from gen-cave.c:1583, which is labyrinth_gen - a generator with alloc -1 that this build never plays at depth 1. dungeon_profile.txt gives depth 1 only 'classic' (alloc 90) and 'modified' (alloc 97). So the previous life's level has 3 or 4 down staircases and 2 or 3 up ones (one of them the one-off where the character arrived). (2) THE M MAP CANNOT HIDE A STAIRCASE: display_map (src/ui-map.c:761) keeps a priority array and only overwrites a cell when the new square has a HIGHER priority, and terrain.txt gives both LESS and MORE priority 25 - the highest of any terrain (floor 5, open door 15, closed door 17, store 20). So a remembered down staircase is always drawn on the M map, and 'no > on the M map' is evidence, not a failure of the instrument. (3) THE M MAP IS THE WHOLE LEVEL, 78x22 cells for 198x66 squares, and it says this level is 81.3 PER CENT UNEXPLORED. I reconstructed it cell by cell: the remembered ground is the northern band (level columns 51-114, rows 0-11) and the eastern half (columns 126-198, rows 3-65); the whole south-west quadrant - columns 0-125, rows 12-65, about 6800 squares - is BLANK. The three remembered up staircases sit at level (64,6), (151,19) and (141,58), which are exactly the three the previous life's report names as 63/6, 149/18 and 139/57, so the reconstruction is right. There is NO remembered down staircase anywhere, which means all 3 or 4 of them are in the 81 per cent nobody has walked - and with 3 or 4 of them and 19 per cent covered, the chance of finding none in what was walked is about 0.2 per cent. THE PLAN: go south-west into the blank quadrant and cover it, because the character stands at level column 50, the north-west corner of it. (ask 754)

note: TWO CALIBRATIONS, both worth a run to have. (1) THE MAP PANEL IS NOT SCROLLED AT ALL HERE: the panel index is the level coordinate. note: THE LOOK CURSOR CANNOT REVEAL AN UNSEEN STAIRCASE, and I checked because it would have been a shortcut worth a hundred asks: target_accept (src/target.c:323) says a terrain feature counts as interesting only when 'square_isknown(cave, grid) && square_isinteresting(player->cave, grid)', and square_isinteresting tests the REAL grid - so the flag is on an unseen staircase but the memory test is not. The look cursor therefore snaps only to remembered stairs, doors, monsters and items, and there is no command anywhere that will walk you to a staircase you have not seen. Coverage is the only discovery route, and the M map plus a digit string is the cheapest coverage there is. (ask 763)

note: THE MAP PANEL IS ONE TO ONE AFTER ALL, AND MY PANEL-COLUMN ARITHMETIC WAS WRONG, not the game. I read the '@' at panel column 49 in two screens by hand and concluded the panel and the M map disagreed by thirteen columns; the '@' is at panel column 35 and the discrepancy was my own count of leading spaces. The check that settles it in one command: python -c on the screen file, find '@' and '<' by string index, and compare their distance with the M map's distance between the same two glyphs. They agree exactly (33 columns = 13 M boxes x 198/78). TWO THINGS THAT FALL OUT: the panel is 1:1 for tiles, so distances WITHIN one screen are exact; and the panel window does not slide smoothly - verify_panel_int (src/ui-output.c:587) scrolls it by HALF A PANEL when the player comes within three squares of an edge, so the panel column is not a level column and the only honest position is the M map, which is fixed on the level. My own note that 'the panel scrolls in jumps and the rows slide differently' was the same fact seen from the wrong side. (ask 766)

note: TWENTY DECISIONS OF SWEEPING, AND THE TECHNIQUE THAT WORKS IS THE DUMB ONE: a digit string along a corridor, and the corridor ends. The aimed walk is dead on this level ('Target Aborted.' - no route to the aimed square), the look-mode walk only moves over ground already known, and the frontier walk (lxg) snaps to the nearest unknown square, which on a one-tile corridor is the tile beside you. So the sweep is: walk to the end of the corridor, turn, walk to the next end, and look at every end, because a corridor end is the shape the generator puts a down staircase on. (ask 774)

note: AN UNKNOWN SCROLL ON THE FLOOR, eleven tiles west, and the decision about it is the first real decision of this life. The pool at depth 1 is eight kinds and I know the weights: Treasure Detection, Phase Door, Light, Detect Invisible and Blessing at fifty each, Deep Descent at twenty, Summon Monster and Darkness at ten each - so eighty-six per cent a useful scroll, seven per cent a Deep Descent that drops me five levels below my deepest (depth 2, so depth 7, on no staircase, with no Phase Door and no Recall), and seven per cent Summon Monster or Darkness. I am going to read it, and here is why, because the reasoning is the part worth recording: the Deep Descent case is NOT a death sentence, because a depth-7 level has one or two UP staircases of its own and the character has survived depth 2 with oil and a whip; the expected loss is about four per cent of the run against a gain of a phase door (the druid's only escape), a blessing, a light, or the identification of a kind that four lives of this family have wanted to know. And the first use of an unknown scroll PAYS EXPERIENCE, which at character level 4 and a kind level of one is nothing and at a kind level of ten is three units. (ask 776)

note: THE TITLE SAYS NOTHING, AND THE SOURCE SAYS WHY: 'You see a Scroll titled quo singrium' - the two words come from names.txt, a list of over a thousand Latin words, and the game picks two of them at random for an unidentified scroll. So the title is not a hint, it is a random pair of words, and 'singrium' means nothing at all. That settles a thing four lives of this family kept half-knowing: the only way to learn what an unidentified object is, apart from the shop that buys that type, is to use it. The scroll is now picked up and the read prompt is open, and the prompt will show me the pack letters so I can read it in one more decision. (ask 777)

note: IT WAS A SCROLL OF DETECT INVISIBLE, and the family now knows one unidentified scroll's kind for the first time in four lives: 'You see no more Scrolls of Detect Invisible'. That is the seventeenth-percent kind, one of the five fifty-weight ones, so the bet was right and the Deep Descent did not happen. TWO THINGS FOR THE NOTEBOOK. First, the read prompt lists the FLOOR as well as the pack ('Read which scroll? (Floor: a-a, ESC)'), so an item can be used where it lies and the pick-up key press was not needed - one decision saved and one less chance to mistype a pack letter. Second, the FIRST USE PAYS NOTHING HERE: the sidebar still reads NXT 26 after the read, and the formula (kind level + your level/2) / your level is (1 + 2) / 4 = 0 for a level-one kind at character level four. The first-use experience is only worth something for a DEEP kind - a Deep Descent at kind level ten would have paid three units, and the Detect Invisible paid none. (ask 779)

note: THE SWEEP TOOL NEEDS ONE RULE I LEARNED THE HARD WAY: every letter on the map is a monster. The chain planner walked the character into a rat and it took four hit points off a 33-point druid with no escape and no Phase Door, so the planner now treats any letter as a wall. A sweep that costs hit points is a bad sweep: the value of this life is the staircase, and a druid at 20 hit points on depth 2 is dead. NXT WENT FROM 26 TO 25, so the fight was worth one experience unit, which at character level four on depth 1 is a quarter of a kill - the level's whole experience argument again. (ask 796)

note: THE CHAIN PLANNER HAS TWO FAILURES AND BOTH ARE WORTH WRITING DOWN. (1) When no unexplored square is reachable from where I stand, it maximises the number of steps and produces a chain that walks down two and up two and down two and up two, twenty-two steps of nothing - a sweep that moves the character nowhere. It has to prefer a path that goes somewhere new over a path that goes far. (2) It walked the character into a rat and four hit points came off, so now every letter on the map is a monster and the planner treats it as a wall. (ask 808)

note: THE CHAIN PLANNER'S THREE LESSONS, all paid for in asks: an unknown square on the map may be a wall, so a chain that STARTS on one moves the character nowhere - sixteen asks of exactly nothing before I saw it; a chain that walks through a pocket in circles is worse than no chain; and the score has to maximise DISTINCT unknown squares, not steps, or the planner walks down two and up two for ever. The other thing this life has settled about the aimed walk: 'Target Aborted.' is textui_target's own message, which means the targeting loop ended without selecting anything - so the digits never moved the cursor, because in the kill-targeting mode a digit picks the next MONSTER and there were none, and the recipe needs 'p' to switch the cursor to free mode where a digit moves it one tile. (ask 841)

note: A DOWN STAIRCASE, ONE TILE WEST OF ME, AND THE FOUR LIVES OF THIS CHARACTER DID NOT FIND ONE. The '>' is at panel column 44 of map row 4 and the '@' is at 45, so the staircase is the tile I am standing next to, and I found it by accident: the aimed walk north that I had just written off as 'Target Aborted' had in fact MOVED ME TEN TILES, and the tenth tile put me beside the staircase. THE AIMED WALK WAS NOT A FAILURE. 'Target Aborted.' is textui_target's message when the targeting loop ends without a selection, and it is printed even though the pathfind inside it had already run - the character had moved ten tiles north and six east, and the message is about the target, not about the walk. Minimaxflash-1.4's measurement of the aimed walk as a lottery with a mean of seventeen tiles was right, and my reading of my own note as 'it does not work on this level' was wrong: it works, it just says 'Target Aborted' when it has nothing to select. The character is High-Elf Druid, character level 4, 33 of 33 hit points, 7 of 7 spell points, armour class 12, 19 flasks of oil, 4 Potions of Cure Light Wounds, 3 gold, no Phase Door and no Recall, and it is going down. A druid's whole fight is this one line of keys, and the reason the class needs it is the armour-class formula: hit_chance is 12 per cent plus 83 per cent of (to-hit minus two thirds of the target's armour class), so a thrown flask at to-hit 11 against the acolyte's armour class 15 is a 19 per cent shot at best, while the whip at to-hit 19 is 51 per cent - and the whip only does two to four damage a blow against eighteen hit points. note: CHARACTER LEVEL 5 IS EIGHTEEN UNITS AWAY: the sheet says Cur Exp 84 and the level 5 threshold for a High-Elf is 101, and the fourth life of this character never got within thirty units of it because every one of its kills was on depth 1, where a kill is worth a quarter of an experience unit. On depth 2 the same kill is worth twice as much, so seven ordinary kills is a level, and that is the first time in four lives that this character has been able to see level 5 from where it stands. THE FULL REST IS FOUR KEYS: R, BACKSPACE, asterisk, ENTER. The rest prompt opens with '& ' already in the field, one backspace deletes the whole field, and the asterisk then means 'until hit points and spell points are full' - and the spell points are the point, because a druid's cloud costs two and the character has one, and a full rest is forty turns for two spell points. (ask 867)

note: THE EQUIPMENT SCREEN EXPLAINS NONE OF IT, and that is the finding: the character is wielding the whip, wearing Soft Leather Armour [8,+0], a Cloak [1,+0] and a Metal Cap [3,+0] - twelve points of armour class, exactly what it has worn all life - and the sidebar says Cur AC 20. Nothing is on the hands, the feet, the arms or the head but the metal cap, and the pack at the last look held a book, rations, oil, potions, a cloak and the Phase Door and no armour. So eight points of armour class arrived between two asks with no visible cause, and the only thing that happened in those two asks was a failed Stinking Cloud and a crow biting the character. The crows are 'B' and they are on the map beside the character and they are biting. A question worth asking of the source and not worth the rest of this life: does the crow - a 'B' - do something to the character's armour class when it bites, or did the character pick up something and put it on without the equipment screen being asked about it? Either way the character is better off than it was, and eight points of armour class is worth a great deal more than the scroll that may have caused it. (ask 871)

note: FEAR IS A CONDITION THAT TAKES THE WEAPON AWAY, and no manual in this repository mentions it: 'You are too afraid to attack the crow!' means the character's attacks do not happen at all while the fear timer runs, so a character that is afraid and surrounded is a character that is being eaten and cannot fight back. The crow's scare blow put it there, and the two crows were biting it down from twenty-five to twenty-two hit points while it could do nothing. So the last potion goes first - a Cure Light Wounds is twenty points and the character is at twenty-two, which is a full character - and then the fear has had a turn to wear off. AND THE ARMOUR CLASS IS STILL 20 WITH NOTHING NEW ON, so it is not the fear and not the crows and not anything in the equipment list, which leaves the game doing something this family has not found before. (ask 874)

note: THE FEAR WAS THE ARMOUR CLASS: while the character was afraid the sidebar said Cur AC 20, and the moment the fear ended - 'You feel bolder now.' - it went back to 12, with the equipment list unchanged the whole time. So being afraid gives a druid eight points of armour class, which is what makes a frightened character so hard to hit, and it is a bargain that looks like a gift and is not: fear blocks the character's attacks entirely ('You are too afraid to attack the crow!') and it cost this life twenty hit points and about eight decisions while two crows ate a character that could not hit back. A SCROLL OF REMOVE FEAR would be worth more to this class than a scroll of Phase Door, and the alchemist does not stock it. THE REST WORKED AS A CURE FOR NOTHING except that it let the timer run: ten turns of rest, two bites, and the fear ended on its own, so the fear in this game is a timer and the only thing that cures it is time. (ask 879)

note: A HUNDRED AND FIFTEEN GOLD PIECES ON THE FLOOR OF DEPTH 2, and it is the single most valuable thing this character has ever held: the alchemist's Phase Door is fifteen, twenty flasks of oil are sixty, two Potions of Cure Light Wounds are forty, and a Scroll of Magic Mapping is sixty-five - so the pile is a whole escape ladder, a full oil supply, the healing this class needs and the scroll that four lives of this family have wanted to buy and could not. THE GOLD PILES ON DEPTH 2 ARE NOT WHAT THE AVERAGE SAYS: the average is nineteen and this one was a hundred and fifteen, so the wealth of a depth is as lumpy as its monsters are. And the character reached it with eight hit points, one spell point and no escape, which is the whole shape of this life: the interesting finds come on the far side of a fight that should not have been survived. (ask 890)
